items.title: Email Campaign · : 1-Year Annual Service (Maintenance Window)
items.preview:
**Audience:** 26 clients at 12-month mark
**List:** Jobber lifecycle trigger (1-year annual service candidates)
### Subject Lines
**Primary:**
`Your 12-month service window is here`
**Alternates:**
1. `Time for your annual checkup (year 1)`
2. `Katy, your system turns 1 this week`
3. `The one appointment that protects everything`
4. `12 months in: here's what happens next`
### Preview Text
`Quick calibration, media check, peace of mind. Book your annual service in 60 seconds.`
### Email Body
---
**Subject:** Your 12-month service window is here
**Preview:** Quick calibration, media check, peace of mind. Book your annual service in 60 seconds.
---
Katy,
Your Re-Ionator Pro Ultra + RO hit the one-year mark last week.
That means it's time for your first annual service: a quick calibration, media inspection, and performance check. Takes about an hour. Keeps your warranty active. Catches small things before they become expensive things.
**What we do:**
- Inspect valves, seals, and media bed depth
- Test backwash cycles and flow rate
- Swap pre-filters and check your RO membrane
- Recalibrate settings if your water chemistry shifted
**Your part:** Pick a day in the next 3 weeks. We'll handle the rest.
[Book Your Annual Service →]
This is the only scheduled touchpoint for the year. After this, you're good until May 2027.
Justin
CEO / ClearWave
P.S. If someone you know is still fighting hard water, rust, or chlorine taste, send them our way. We'll give them a free water assessment, and if they move forward, you'll earn $500 cash (referrals 1; 5), $750 (6; 9), or $1,000 (10+). Even if they just book a consult and don't close, you get a $50 gift card.
---
### Send Timing
**Tuesday, May 6, 2026 at 9:00 AM ET**
(Mid-week, morning, high-intent maintenance action)
### Expected Performance
- **Open rate:** 52; 58% (high-intent transactional trigger, named personalization, clear utility)
- **Click rate:** 12; 18% (single clear CTA, no friction, expected expense)
- **Conversion (booked service):** 60; 70% of clickers (15 of 26 likely to book within 7 days)
**Justification:**
This is a **required maintenance trigger** with contractual/warranty weight. It's transactional, not promotional. Personalization (name, system, city) is trivial via Jobber merge tags. Mailchimp avg open is 41%; this will significantly exceed because it's 1:1 relevant and time-bound. Recent campaigns had <1% click because they were educational/abstract; this has a concrete next step tied to a known obligation.
**IDEA_SOURCING.md compliance:**
- **Lifecycle trigger (Jobber):** Annual service window is the #1 highest-intent, highest-conversion moment post-install.
- **Personalization at scale:** Name, system, city from Jobber.
- **Referral plug (non-invasive):** Bonus structure in P.S., does not dilute primary CTA.
---

items.title: Email Campaign · : Cold Lead Re-Engagement (Water News Hook)
items.preview:
**Audience:** 1,000 cold subscribers (no engagement >60 days, never reached quote stage)
**List:** Mailchimp segment (cold leads)
### Subject Lines
**Primary:**
`The EPA just changed the lead rule`
**Alternates:**
1. `New federal water regs hit Virginia this fall`
2. `What the new lead limits mean for your home`
3. `Testing alone won't fix this (new EPA rule)`
4. `You asked about water 3 months ago. Here's why it matters now.`
### Preview Text
`New lead limits took effect April 2026. Here's what changed and what you can do about it.`
### Email Body
---
**Subject:** The EPA just changed the lead rule
**Preview:** New lead limits took effect April 2026. Here's what changed and what you can do about it.
---
You reached out a few months ago about your water.
Life got busy. I get it.
But something changed last month that's worth 90 seconds of your time.
**The EPA's new Lead and Copper Rule took effect April 29, 2026.**
The old action level was 15 parts per billion. The new trigger is 10 ppb, and utilities now have to replace lead service lines within 10 years (not 30).
**Translation:** If you're in an older neighborhood (pre-1986 plumbing, pre-1950s service lines), your risk profile just got flagged at the federal level.
Testing tells you if you have a problem. It doesn't solve it.
**A point-of-entry filtration system does both.**
If you want to know what's actually in your water and whether you need to do anything about it, we'll come out and run a free water assessment. No lab fees, no sales pitch if the water's fine, no obligation.
Takes 20 minutes. You'll know exactly what you're drinking, bathing in, and cooking with.
[Book Your Free Water Assessment →]
Justin
CEO / ClearWave
P.S. If you're not interested right now, no worries. But if you know a family member, neighbor, or coworker who's dealing with hard water, staining, or taste issues, send them our way. If they move forward, you'll earn $500 cash. If they just book a consult, you get a $50 gift card.
---
### Send Timing
**Thursday, May 8, 2026 at 10:00 AM ET**
(Mid-week, mid-morning, news-cycle relevance still fresh)
### Expected Performance
- **Open rate:** 28; 34% (news hook, regulatory authority, segment is cold so baseline is lower)
- **Click rate:** 2; 4% (realistic for re-engagement; 20; 40 clicks)
- **Conversion (booked assessment):** 15; 25% of clickers (3; 10 booked assessments)
**Justification:**
Cold leads are **low-intent by definition**, so we're not expecting the 41% house-list open rate. But a **timely, external news hook** (EPA rule change is real, recent, and relevant to VA/MD/DC audience) resets the conversation without sounding desperate ("still interested?"). The **new lead rule is a legitimate forcing function** and positions ClearWave as educator-first, not seller-first.
Recent campaigns to the ALL audience had 0.4; 0.6% open and 0.00; 0.01% click because they were abstract ("maintenance truth," "how long should it last"). This has **a concrete external event** and a **no-risk next step** (free water assessment).
Even if we convert 5 cold leads to booked assessments, and 2 of those close at avg $8,000 invoice, that's $16,000 revenue from a list that was otherwise dormant.
**IDEA_SOURCING.md compliance:**
- **Regulatory/seasonal forcing function:** New EPA rule is a timely, credible hook (similar to "32k gallons jet fuel" but with personal relevance, not abstract fear).
- **Re-engagement best practice:** Lead with new value, not "hey, remember us?" Frame it as "here's what changed in YOUR world."
- **Free water assessment as the only CTA:** Hard rule compliance, exact phrase.
---
## Why These Two (and Not Others)
**Annual Service (26)** is the highest-conversion, highest-AOV opportunity this week. It's transactional, time-bound, and expected. Conversion rate will be 10; 20× higher than any nurture email.
**Cold Lead Re-Engagement (1,000)** is the highest-volume opportunity to reactivate dead leads without burning goodwill. The EPA hook is fresh, relevant, and positions Justin as educator (not desperate closer).
**Why NOT the others this week:**
- **Referral push (17):** Good candidates, but referral emails historically underperform unless paired with a forcing function (holiday, milestone, or incentive expiration). Better to layer into the annual service P.S. or save for a summer "refer 3, win a Yeti" promo.
- **RO replacement (25):** Solid, but lower urgency than annual service. RO membranes don't fail catastrophically; they degrade slowly. Better as a **secondary send next week** after annual service clears.
- **Concierge upsell (100):** High volume, decent intent, but requires more education/math. Better as a **stand-alone 3-email sequence** (not a one-off). Propose separately if you want a Concierge nurture track.
---
**Ready to load into Mailchimp?** I can generate the Jobber merge-tag syntax and segment filters if you want to go live this week.

---
